- Relaxation Runge-Kutta (RRK) in `fd.ERK`: `relax=` makes every step conserve an entropy $\eta$, or change it by exactly $\gamma \Delta t \sum_i b_i \langle \eta'(U_i), k_i \rangle$, and advances the time by $\gamma \Delta t$, which keeps the order (Ketcheson 2019, Ranocha et al. 2020). The entropy is a symmetric matrix or constant bilinear form $E$ ($\eta = \tfrac12 u^T E u$, $\gamma$ in closed form), a functional Form of the unknown (derivative by the complex step), a pair `(eta, grad)` of callables, or `eta` alone for an entropy that $f$ conserves. `relax_solver="auto"`, `"newton"`, `"secant"` or `"brent"` chooses the root solver, all in C++ (`ExplicitRK::step_relaxed`, `Entropy`, `RelaxOptions`, `RelaxInfo` in `timestep/explicit_rk.hpp`). Newton and the secant method solve $r(\gamma)/\gamma = 0$, which removes the trivial root $\gamma = 0$, and stop once the residual has reached the rounding level of $\eta$, since $r' = O(\Delta t^2)$ fixes $\gamma$ only to about $\epsilon |\eta| / \Delta t^2$. `relax_tol`, `relax_maxiter`, `relax_time="idt"` or `"fixed"`, `step(u, relax=False)`, `rk.gamma` and `rk.relax_info` (`fd.RelaxInfo`). A step without a positive root raises and leaves `u` unchanged. On KdV with cubic splines the $L^2$ norm stays at $10^{-14}$ over 2000 steps of RK4 instead of drifting by $1.7 \cdot 10^{-10}$, with one or two Newton iterations per step (`tests/cpp/test_explicit_rk.cpp`, `tests/python/test_rrk.py`). Manual 7.9, reference G.10.
- Relaxation in `fd.SSPRK` and `fd.IRK` as well, with the same arguments as `fd.ERK`, and `relax_conserved=` for all three. The relaxation is now one class for every Runge-Kutta step, `femd::Relaxation` in the new `timestep/relaxation.hpp` (`begin`, `stage(U_i, k_i, b_i)`, `finish(u, dt)`), used by `ExplicitRK::step_relaxed`, `SSPRK::step_relaxed` and `ImplicitRK::step_relaxed`. `fd.SSPRK` records the stages of its Shu-Osher form with the Butcher weights of each method (`SSPRK::weights()`), needs order 2 or more and refuses a limiter. `fd.IRK` relaxes the converged stages in 1D and 2D and refuses boundary data. `relax_conserved=True` takes the stage sum as zero, so a conserved entropy returns to its old value whatever error the stages carry: for KdV with Gauss 2, simplified Newton and `tol=1e-6` the $L^2$ drift over 50 steps falls from $7 \cdot 10^{-9}$ to $10^{-15}$. Radau IIA relaxed conserves what it otherwise dissipates. Forward Euler (in `ERK` and `SSPRK`) is refused, as its relaxation equation has only the root 0 (`tests/cpp/test_ssp_rk.cpp`, `test_implicit_rk.cpp`, `tests/python/test_rrk.py`). Manual 7.7, 7.8, 7.9, reference G.6, G.8, G.10.
